story.title: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward

facts.text: A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis.

Suing on behalf of the NAACP, the Southern Environmental Law Center said the AI company had “installed and operated at least 35 combustion turbines and other sources of air pollution at the Colossus site without ever obtaining the necessary preconstruction or operating air permits.” It also accused xAI of violating the Clean Air Act.
“Our position has been clear: xAI cannot operate gas turbines without the required permits.”

In a statement , the NAACP’s director of environmental and climate justice Abre’ Connor described this as “another important victory in our effort to hold xAI accountable.” (A similar motion to dismiss from the Department of Justice was denied earlier this month )

Focusing on xAI’s claim that these kinds of citizen lawsuits are unconstitutional, Judge Brown wrote, “Because citizen suit plaintiffs sue on their own behalf, in their own name, and seek penalties that redress harm to themselves, they are not exercising the federal government’s executive power.”

A federal judge in Mississippi has rejected an effort by the Trump administration to shut down a lawsuit brought by the NAACP against Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence company, xAI, allowing a closely watched environmental justice case to continue.
The ruling keeps the NAACP’s challenge alive while allowing the federal government to remain involved.

The lawsuit, filed by the national NAACP and its Mississippi State Conference, accuses xAI and its subsidiary, MZX Tech, of operating a gas-fired power plant in Southaven, Mississippi, without the environmental permits required under the Clean Air Act.
The NAACP later asked the court for emergency action to stop what it described as ongoing unpermitted pollution.
A federal judge just handed the NAACP a major victory in its fight against xAI, allowing a lawsuit alleging Clean Air Act violations at the company's data center to move forward.

Data centers have become flashpoints in communities across the country as residents push back against facilities they see as bringing pollution, noise, and strain on local power grids without commensurate benefits.
The judge's decision to let the case proceed past preliminary motions means xAI will now face discovery and potentially a trial on the merits of the NAACP's claims.

passages: Binance was hacked with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, raising questions about the recovery of stolen funds and the broader fallout for crypto markets.
Around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets have been frozen so far, according to a Binance security update .

Assuming frozen stablecoins are eventually returned, Binance's SAFU emergency fund, worth approximately $1.2 billion, could cover roughly a third of the remaining losses, with the balance coming from the exchange's own funds.

Chainalysis also pointed to North Korea , with co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin saying the firm assessed that the $6.4 billion Binance hack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor, citing links to previous attacks.
The firm estimated that approximately $6.36 billion in digital assets were moved from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains, with most transferred within about 20 minutes.
The FBI previously identified the same group as responsible for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, according to the company's insights.
"The most important takeaway for markets is that this does not currently appear to create meaningful solvency risk for Binance," Farrell said.

Speaking to CNBC's " Squawk Box Asia ," Perkins said the industry must address cybersecurity challenges to reach its full potential, calling for stronger defenses and policies to hold cybercriminals accountable.
"A freeze stops the money from moving, and recovery follows through legal process," Redbord told CNBC.
A technical freeze may happen quickly, while returning funds can take months or years," Jardine told CNBC.
TRM Labs said the Binance attack shared characteristics with previous North Korea-linked incidents, including preparations made well before the theft and transaction signatures obtained in advance.
Farrell said the key indicators to watch were how quickly Binance resumes withdrawals and whether outflows remain orderly.
He added that a shortfall in customer assets could force the exchange to sell reserves, potentially triggering broader selling across crypto markets.
The Binance hack underscores the need for stronger cybersecurity standards and greater coordination among governments, according to Chris Perkins, head of Franklin Crypto at Franklin Templeton.

extraction.body: Binance was hacked with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, raising questions about the recovery of stolen funds and the broader fallout for crypto markets. Around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets have been frozen so far, according to a Binance security update . The exchange pledged to cover all losses, while blockchain investigators linked the attack to North Korea and analysts assessed the potential financial risks. Bitcoin was under pressure on Friday and was trading below $78,000. Freezing cryptocurrency prevents it from being transferred, but recovering the funds requires a separate legal process, according to Ari Redbord, global head of policy at blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs and a former U.S. federal prosecutor and Treasury official. "A freeze stops the money from moving, and recovery follows through legal process," Redbord told CNBC. Redbord said law enforcement typically obtains a court order or seizure warrant before working with stablecoin issuers to release or reissue assets and return them to their rightful owners. "Stablecoins are the most recoverable asset class in crypto because the issuer controls the token contract," he said. "Tether and Circle can freeze, burn and reissue, which allows frozen USDT and USDC to be returned to a victim." But recovering bitcoin and ether is more challenging because they have no issuer that can directly freeze the assets. Instead, investigators must trace funds through exchanges and other crypto services where they can potentially be intercepted, added Redbord. Eric Jardine, head of research at blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, said returning frozen assets requires coordination among law enforcement, exchanges and token issuers. "There is no standard recovery timeline. A technical freeze may happen quickly, while returning funds can take months or years," Jardine told CNBC. Jardine added that while bitcoin and ether cannot be frozen by an issuer, they can still be traced and potentially recovered. Investigators can trace the funds on public blockchains and intervene when they reach a cooperating exchange or another centralized platform, he said. TRM Labs attributed the attack with high confidence to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit, based on on-chain and off-chain intelligence. The FBI previously identified the same group as responsible for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, according to the company's insights. TRM Labs said the Binance attack shared characteristics with previous North Korea-linked incidents, including preparations made well before the theft and transaction signatures obtained in advance. The firm estimated that approximately $6.36 billion in digital assets were moved from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains, with most transferred within about 20 minutes. TRM Labs said preparations for the attack began at least 36 hours before the theft, with the attackers using Tornado Cash, a cryptocurrency mixing service, to fund their wallets ahead of the breach. Chainalysis also pointed to North Korea , with co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin saying the firm assessed that the $6.4 billion Binance hack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor, citing links to previous attacks. The attack does not currently appear to pose a significant solvency risk for Binance, according to Sean Farrell, head of digital asset strategy at Fundstrat Global Advisors. "The most important takeaway for markets is that this does not currently appear to create meaningful solvency risk for Binance," Farrell said. Farrell estimated that around $3.3 billion in assets remained unfrozen. Assuming frozen stablecoins are eventually returned, Binance's SAFU emergency fund, worth approximately $1.2 billion, could cover roughly a third of the remaining losses, with the balance coming from the exchange's own funds. Farrell said the key indicators to watch were how quickly Binance resumes withdrawals and whether outflows remain orderly. He added that a shortfall in customer assets could force the exchange to sell reserves, potentially triggering broader selling across crypto markets. "I do not think that is the setup we are dealing with, but the key tell will be how quickly withdrawals resume and whether outflows stay orderly," Farrell said. The Binance hack underscores the need for stronger cybersecurity standards and greater coordination among governments, according to Chris Perkins, head of Franklin Crypto at Franklin Templeton. Speaking to CNBC's " Squawk Box Asia ," Perkins said the industry must address cybersecurity challenges to reach its full potential, calling for stronger defenses and policies to hold cybercriminals accountable. "We need to make sure standards are incredibly high, but we have to really focus on the criminals," Perkins said. Perkins called for greater international cooperation to address cybersecurity threats, pointing to regulatory coordination among G20 countries following the global financial crisis as a potential model. He also said AI could help improve cybersecurity by identifying and addressing vulnerabilities, even as the technology is used by both attackers and defenders. Got a confidential news tip? extraction.body: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has reportedly suffered a major cyberattack, with hackers stealing cryptocurrencies worth $6.3 billion in what could be the biggest crypto heist in history. Confirming the incident, Binance said it was working to contain and resolve what it described as a "complex attack". The exchange said it was coordinating with law enforcement agencies and other industry partners to trace and freeze the stolen assets. "This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance wrote in a post on X. The exchange also cautioned that the estimated value of the stolen assets could rise further as investigations continue. The $6.3-billion figure may "continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets," it said. Here's what we know about the reported Binance hack so far. What Happened? $6.3 Billion In Cryptocurrency Stolen According to Binance, around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrencies were stolen from wallets used by the exchange to process transactions. In its initial assessment, the company believed the attack had originated from a compromised laptop. However, further investigation revealed additional security breaches. "However, our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach," Binance said. The attack targeted Binance.com, the exchange's global centralised platform. Binance.US, which serves customers in the United States, was not affected, the company said. Binance said the compromised laptop provided the attacker with access to a service container, enabling the submission of unauthorised withdrawal transactions. Richard Teng, Binance's co-chief executive officer, described the incident as a "complex attack process". According to US-based blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs, the attackers compromised Binance's "signing infrastructure", which authorises transactions. This allegedly allowed them to issue instructions that drained the affected wallets. ALSO READ: Mohan Yadav Announces 2% DA Hike From January 2026 For MP Govt Employees Blockchain records indicate that the bulk of the heist took place within approximately 20 minutes. After moving the funds, the attackers attempted to transfer them beyond the reach of Binance's counterparties and stablecoin issuers. These entities have since frozen roughly half of the stolen assets. Binance and other authorities have not confirmed the identity of those responsible for the attack. However, US-based blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs has attributed the hack to a North Korean-linked group known as TraderTraitor, which it described as one of North Korea's elite hacking units. In a post on its website on Thursday, TRM said: "We make this judgment with high confidence." Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis also pointed towards the same group. Its co-founder and CEO, Jonathan Levin, wrote on X that the Binance hack was "likely done by DPRK (North Korea) group TraderTraitor". Binance said on Friday that it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to manage the fallout from the attack. This includes $5 billion already held in the affected token assets. In an earlier statement, Teng said users' funds were safe. As a precautionary measure, the exchange also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals. The company said it was working with its partners to freeze assets worth $3 billion that have been traced so far. However, freezing the assets does not necessarily mean they will be returned to Binance. It does, nevertheless, restrict the hackers' ability to convert the stolen cryptocurrencies into cash. Binance also said it remained on schedule to restore withdrawal services. "We are still on track towards the expected timeline to resume the withdrawal service in 45 hours," the exchange said. ALSO READ: Money Matters: Why Financial Conversations Remain Taboo In Indian Households

passages: Here's what we know about the hack, possible North Korean involvement and Binance's investigation.
Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said Friday that hackers stole more than $6 billion in what appears to be the largest cryptocurrency heist on record.
Blockchain firms have pointed to the attack coming from a North Korean hacking unit.
Blockchain analysis company Chainalysis also believed the Binance hack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor, its co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin wrote on X.
Gox have had a more substantial impact in terms of the bitcoin amount affected, he said.
Asked whether North Korea was involved, Trump said: "We're looking at that."
"An attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes," TRM said.
"Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists."

Asked about the potential ties to North Korea, a Binance spokesperson said only that the company is "working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of the criminals and bring them to justice."
In February of last year, another cryptocurrency exchange, Bybit, suffered a $1.5 billion hit when it was hacked.
The FBI said North Korea and TraderTraitor were responsible for the hack.
Binance worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets.
"Cyber threats are becoming more sophisticated and widespread as ever, and it is likely only a matter of time before an even larger hack, with even greater financial fallout, makes headlines."
"We are working nonstop to resolve this," Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said Friday in a video posted to X.
Binance said on X that an initial investigation suggested the incident may have involved a compromised laptop, but that a subsequent investigation uncovered additional "points of breach."

"This looks like one signature that gave the attacker a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet," he said, referring to cryptocurrency wallets that hold users' "private keys," or unique authorizations, digitally and that are connected to the internet.
"User assets are held under Binance's established security architecture," he said.
"The vast majority sits in cold wallets" — which are offline and used for secure storage — "and are only moved into a hot wallet when a user makes withdrawal."
Left: Binance logo and hacker code are seen in this illustration taken Oct.
Binance has said deposits were unaffected, while withdrawals have been suspended and are expected to resume in the next day or two.

Experts have said that North Korea turned to crypto hacking and other illicit cyber activities in recent years as a source of badly needed foreign currency to support its troubled economy and fund its nuclear program in the wake of tough U.N. sanctions and other difficulties.

extraction.body: Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said Friday that hackers stole more than $6 billion in what appears to be the largest cryptocurrency heist on record. Blockchain firms have pointed to the attack coming from a North Korean hacking unit. The company said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the stolen assets and was beginning to recover assets for users. Binance worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets. WATCH: $6 billion cryptocurrency heist puts investors on edge The cryptocurrency exchange has promised to cover all losses, and it has been sharing regular updates on its social media channels as it uncovers more information about the hack. "We are working nonstop to resolve this," Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said Friday in a video posted to X. In an exchange Friday with reporters at the White House, President Donald Trump said U.S. officials were investigating the Binance hack. Asked whether North Korea was involved, Trump said: "We're looking at that." Here's what we know about the hack, possible North Korean involvement and Binance's investigation. Binance said on X that an initial investigation suggested the incident may have involved a compromised laptop, but that a subsequent investigation uncovered additional "points of breach." U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm TRM, in a post on its website late Thursday, attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, which it described as North Korea's elite hacking unit. "We make this judgment with high confidence," the firm said. "An attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes," TRM said. "Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists." Blockchain analysis company Chainalysis also believed the Binance hack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor, its co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin wrote on X. Asked about the potential ties to North Korea, a Binance spokesperson said only that the company is "working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of the criminals and bring them to justice." Experts have said that North Korea turned to crypto hacking and other illicit cyber activities in recent years as a source of badly needed foreign currency to support its troubled economy and fund its nuclear program in the wake of tough U.N. sanctions and other difficulties. In December 2022, South Korea's spy agency said North Korean hackers had stolen an estimated 1.5 trillion won ($1.1 billion) in cryptocurrency and other virtual assets over the past five years, more than half of it in 2022 alone. It said North Korea's capacity to steal digital assets was considered among the world's best. While about half of the stolen assets were frozen, there is evidence that the hackers already are transferring and converting some of what wasn't recovered, said Garrick Hileman, an independent cryptocurrency analyst. "Like in money laundering, you bring in the stolen goods and launder those through a mixer or tumbler," he said. "You mix it in with other cryptos, and it's harder to track." TRM and several other crypto firms and experts have said the hack represents the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. In February of last year, another cryptocurrency exchange, Bybit, suffered a $1.5 billion hit when it was hacked. The FBI said North Korea and TraderTraitor were responsible for the hack. TRM listed the Bybit hack when it referenced similarities between the Binance hack and previous attacks linked to TraderTraitor. Binance's founder, Changpeng Zhao, wrote on X that while Binance's hack might be the largest in terms of its dollar value, previous attacks on other companies like the crypto exchange Mt. Gox have had a more substantial impact in terms of the bitcoin amount affected, he said. Experts warn this scale of hacking could become more commonplace. "A cyber attack of this level is a matter of when, not if, particularly alongside the rise of AI," said Andy Ward, a senior vice president at Absolute Security. "Cyber threats are becoming more sophisticated and widespread as ever, and it is likely only a matter of time before an even larger hack, with even greater financial fallout, makes headlines." The hack has raised questions about why stronger approval controls were not in place, said Kok Tin Gan, co-founder and CEO of cybersecurity firm NyxLab. "This looks like one signature that gave the attacker a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet," he said, referring to cryptocurrency wallets that hold users' "private keys," or unique authorizations, digitally and that are connected to the internet. Teng, Binance's co-CEO, confirmed in a nearly five-minute video posted on X Friday that Binance's own hot wallet was affected. "User assets are held under Binance's established security architecture," he said. "The vast majority sits in cold wallets" — which are offline and used for secure storage — "and are only moved into a hot wallet when a user makes withdrawal." Teng said Binance's tech and security teams are "still deep" in investigating the hack. He said it was not carried out by one person and that the attackers used complex tactics, including a "self-destruct mechanism" that is making the incident more difficult to investigate. "We are working with law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, token issuers and other exchanges to trace and recover stolen funds," Teng said. "We will do everything within our power to make sure that these bad actors will be held accountable." Binance has said deposits were unaffected, while withdrawals have been suspended and are expected to resume in the next day or two. Associated Press journalists John Seewer, Aamer Madhani, Hyung-jin Kim and Kim Tong-hyung contributed to this report. Support trusted journalism and civil dialogue. coreStoryFacts.text: Binance was hacked with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, raising questions about the recovery of stolen funds and the broader fallout for crypto markets.
Around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets have been frozen so far, according to a Binance security update .

Assuming frozen stablecoins are eventually returned, Binance's SAFU emergency fund, worth approximately $1.2 billion, could cover roughly a third of the remaining losses, with the balance coming from the exchange's own funds.

Chainalysis also pointed to North Korea , with co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin saying the firm assessed that the $6.4 billion Binance hack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor, citing links to previous attacks.
The firm estimated that approximately $6.36 billion in digital assets were moved from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains, with most transferred within about 20 minutes.

extraction.body: Binance was hacked with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, raising questions about the recovery of stolen funds and the broader fallout for crypto markets. Around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets have been frozen so far, according to a Binance security update . The exchange pledged to cover all losses, while blockchain investigators linked the attack to North Korea and analysts assessed the potential financial risks. Bitcoin was under pressure on Friday and was trading below $78,000. Freezing cryptocurrency prevents it from being transferred, but recovering the funds requires a separate legal process, according to Ari Redbord, global head of policy at blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs and a former U.S. federal prosecutor and Treasury official. "A freeze stops the money from moving, and recovery follows through legal process," Redbord told CNBC. Redbord said law enforcement typically obtains a court order or seizure warrant before working with stablecoin issuers to release or reissue assets and return them to their rightful owners. "Stablecoins are the most recoverable asset class in crypto because the issuer controls the token contract," he said. "Tether and Circle can freeze, burn and reissue, which allows frozen USDT and USDC to be returned to a victim." But recovering bitcoin and ether is more challenging because they have no issuer that can directly freeze the assets. Instead, investigators must trace funds through exchanges and other crypto services where they can potentially be intercepted, added Redbord. Eric Jardine, head of research at blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, said returning frozen assets requires coordination among law enforcement, exchanges and token issuers. "There is no standard recovery timeline. A technical freeze may happen quickly, while returning funds can take months or years," Jardine told CNBC. Jardine added that while bitcoin and ether cannot be frozen by an issuer, they can still be traced and potentially recovered. Investigators can trace the funds on public blockchains and intervene when they reach a cooperating exchange or another centralized platform, he said. TRM Labs attributed the attack with high confidence to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit, based on on-chain and off-chain intelligence. The FBI previously identified the same group as responsible for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, according to the company's insights. TRM Labs said the Binance attack shared characteristics with previous North Korea-linked incidents, including preparations made well before the theft and transaction signatures obtained in advance. The firm estimated that approximately $6.36 billion in digital assets were moved from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains, with most transferred within about 20 minutes. TRM Labs said preparations for the attack began at least 36 hours before the theft, with the attackers using Tornado Cash, a cryptocurrency mixing service, to fund their wallets ahead of the breach. Chainalysis also pointed to North Korea , with co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin saying the firm assessed that the $6.4 billion Binance hack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor, citing links to previous attacks. The attack does not currently appear to pose a significant solvency risk for Binance, according to Sean Farrell, head of digital asset strategy at Fundstrat Global Advisors. "The most important takeaway for markets is that this does not currently appear to create meaningful solvency risk for Binance," Farrell said. Farrell estimated that around $3.3 billion in assets remained unfrozen. extraction.body: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has reportedly suffered a major cyberattack, with hackers stealing cryptocurrencies worth $6.3 billion in what could be the biggest crypto heist in history. Confirming the incident, Binance said it was working to contain and resolve what it described as a "complex attack". The exchange said it was coordinating with law enforcement agencies and other industry partners to trace and freeze the stolen assets. "This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance wrote in a post on X. The exchange also cautioned that the estimated value of the stolen assets could rise further as investigations continue. The $6.3-billion figure may "continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets," it said. Here's what we know about the reported Binance hack so far. What Happened? $6.3 Billion In Cryptocurrency Stolen According to Binance, around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrencies were stolen from wallets used by the exchange to process transactions. In its initial assessment, the company believed the attack had originated from a compromised laptop. However, further investigation revealed additional security breaches. "However, our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach," Binance said. The attack targeted Binance.com, the exchange's global centralised platform. Binance.US, which serves customers in the United States, was not affected, the company said. Binance said the compromised laptop provided the attacker with access to a service container, enabling the submission of unauthorised withdrawal transactions. Richard Teng, Binance's co-chief executive officer, described the incident as a "complex attack process". According to US-based blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs, the attackers compromised Binance's "signing infrastructure", which authorises transactions. This allegedly allowed them to issue instructions that drained the affected wallets. ALSO READ: Mohan Yadav Announces 2% DA Hike From January 2026 For MP Govt Employees Blockchain records indicate that the bulk of the heist took place within approximately 20 minutes. After moving the funds, the attackers attempted to transfer them beyond the reach of Binance's counterparties and stablecoin issuers. These entities have since frozen roughly half of the stolen assets. Binance and other authorities have not confirmed the identity of those responsible for the attack. However, US-based blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs has attributed the hack to a North Korean-linked group known as TraderTraitor, which it described as one of North Korea's elite hacking units. In a post on its website on Thursday, TRM said: "We make this judgment with high confidence." Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis also pointed towards the same group. Its co-founder and CEO, Jonathan Levin, wrote on X that the Binance hack was "likely done by DPRK (North Korea) group TraderTraitor". Binance said on Friday that it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to manage the fallout from the attack. This includes $5 billion already held in the affected token assets. In an earlier statement, Teng said users' funds were safe. As a precautionary measure, the exchange also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals. The company said it was working with its partners to freeze assets worth $3 billion that have been traced so far. However, freezing the assets does not necessarily mean they will be returned to Binance. It does, nevertheless, restrict the hackers' ability to convert the stolen cryptocurrencies into cash. Binance also said it remained on schedule to restore withdrawal services. "We are still on track towards the expected timeline to resume the withdrawal service in 45 hours," the exchange said. ALSO READ: Money Matters: Why Financial Conversations Remain Taboo In Indian Households

passages: Here's what we know about the hack, possible North Korean involvement and Binance's investigation.
Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said Friday that hackers stole more than $6 billion in what appears to be the largest cryptocurrency heist on record.
Blockchain firms have pointed to the attack coming from a North Korean hacking unit.
Blockchain analysis company Chainalysis also believed the Binance hack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor, its co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin wrote on X.
Gox have had a more substantial impact in terms of the bitcoin amount affected, he said.
Asked whether North Korea was involved, Trump said: "We're looking at that."
"An attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes," TRM said.
"Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists."

Asked about the potential ties to North Korea, a Binance spokesperson said only that the company is "working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of the criminals and bring them to justice."
In February of last year, another cryptocurrency exchange, Bybit, suffered a $1.5 billion hit when it was hacked.
The FBI said North Korea and TraderTraitor were responsible for the hack.
Binance worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets.
"Cyber threats are becoming more sophisticated and widespread as ever, and it is likely only a matter of time before an even larger hack, with even greater financial fallout, makes headlines."
"We are working nonstop to resolve this," Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said Friday in a video posted to X.
Binance said on X that an initial investigation suggested the incident may have involved a compromised laptop, but that a subsequent investigation uncovered additional "points of breach."

"This looks like one signature that gave the attacker a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet," he said, referring to cryptocurrency wallets that hold users' "private keys," or unique authorizations, digitally and that are connected to the internet.
"User assets are held under Binance's established security architecture," he said.
"The vast majority sits in cold wallets" — which are offline and used for secure storage — "and are only moved into a hot wallet when a user makes withdrawal."
Left: Binance logo and hacker code are seen in this illustration taken Oct.
Binance has said deposits were unaffected, while withdrawals have been suspended and are expected to resume in the next day or two.

Experts have said that North Korea turned to crypto hacking and other illicit cyber activities in recent years as a source of badly needed foreign currency to support its troubled economy and fund its nuclear program in the wake of tough U.N. sanctions and other difficulties.

facts.text: Binance was hacked with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, raising questions about the recovery of stolen funds and the broader fallout for crypto markets.
Around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets have been frozen so far, according to a Binance security update .

Assuming frozen stablecoins are eventually returned, Binance's SAFU emergency fund, worth approximately $1.2 billion, could cover roughly a third of the remaining losses, with the balance coming from the exchange's own funds.

Chainalysis also pointed to North Korea , with co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin saying the firm assessed that the $6.4 billion Binance hack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor, citing links to previous attacks.
The firm estimated that approximately $6.36 billion in digital assets were moved from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains, with most transferred within about 20 minutes.
The FBI previously identified the same group as responsible for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, according to the company's insights.
"The most important takeaway for markets is that this does not currently appear to create meaningful solvency risk for Binance," Farrell said.

Speaking to CNBC's " Squawk Box Asia ," Perkins said the industry must address cybersecurity challenges to reach its full potential, calling for stronger defenses and policies to hold cybercriminals accountable.
"A freeze stops the money from moving, and recovery follows through legal process," Redbord told CNBC.
A technical freeze may happen quickly, while returning funds can take months or years," Jardine told CNBC.
TRM Labs said the Binance attack shared characteristics with previous North Korea-linked incidents, including preparations made well before the theft and transaction signatures obtained in advance.
Farrell said the key indicators to watch were how quickly Binance resumes withdrawals and whether outflows remain orderly.
He added that a shortfall in customer assets could force the exchange to sell reserves, potentially triggering broader selling across crypto markets.
The Binance hack underscores the need for stronger cybersecurity standards and greater coordination among governments, according to Chris Perkins, head of Franklin Crypto at Franklin Templeton.

The incident raises an important question for millions of people who hold Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies on Binance: Could they lose their money because of the hack?135348042Binance has assured customers that their funds are safe and that it will cover all losses arising from the incident.
Binance wallets on Bitcoin, Tron, Solana, XRP Ledger and several other networks also transferred funds to addresses controlled by the attacker.

extraction.body: Binance hacked: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, has suffered a massive security breach in which hackers moved approximately $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from its wallets. The attack, which took place on October 29, is being described as the biggest cryptocurrency theft in history. The scale of the incident has raised concerns among cryptocurrency investors. Blockchain investigators have linked the attack to North Korea, while Binance says it has managed to freeze a substantial portion of the affected assets. The incident raises an important question for millions of people who hold Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies on Binance: Could they lose their money because of the hack?135348042Binance has assured customers that their funds are safe and that it will cover all losses arising from the incident. The exchange has also been working with blockchain companies, cryptocurrency issuers and law enforcement agencies to trace and recover the stolen assets.Will you lose your Bitcoin if Binance gets hacked?This is perhaps the biggest concern for Binance customers following the incident. The short answer is that customers do not automatically lose their Bitcoin or other cryptocurrency because of this security breach.Binance has repeatedly assured users that their funds are safe. The exchange has also promised to cover all losses arising from the incident using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and its own funds. The company has not reported evidence that customers' individual account passwords or wallet private keys were leaked in the incident. However, the attack has raised questions about how cryptocurrency exchanges store and protect customer assets.Most large exchanges use hot wallets to process transactions and withdrawals. For investors, the incident is a reminder that holding cryptocurrency on an exchange carries a different set of risks from holding it in a personal wallet.Customers should also be aware that Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals on several networks while it investigated the incident and strengthened its security systems. The exchange said deposits were unaffected and withdrawals were expected to resume within the next day or two.Binance's $1 billion SAFU fund: Is it enough to cover the losses?Binance maintains a Secure Asset Fund for Users, commonly known as SAFU, to protect customers in exceptional circumstances. The fund is worth approximately $1 billion and is designed to provide an additional layer of protection for users.However, the estimated $6.3 billion impact of the latest incident is significantly higher than the fund's reported value.Binance has therefore said it will also use its own resources to cover the losses. This means customers are not expected to bear the financial burden of the incident, according to the exchange's assurance.The next important development will be Binance's updated proof-of-reserves report, which should help investors assess the exchange's asset backing following the incident.Who hacked Binance and stole $6.3 billion?Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs has attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a hacking unit associated with North Korea. The firm said it reached this conclusion with high confidence after examining on-chain transactions and other intelligence. According to TRM Labs, the attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets across 10 different blockchain networks. Most of the transfers took place within around 20 minutes.TraderTraitor is a North Korean hacking operation known for targeting cryptocurrency platforms and digital asset companies. The group has been linked to several major cryptocurrency thefts. The suspected involvement of North Korean hackers is particularly significant because the country has repeatedly been accused of using cyberattacks to generate funds. Its hacking operations have targeted cryptocurrency exchanges, financial institutions and blockchain projects.The group was also linked to the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, which was previously considered the biggest cryptocurrency theft on record. Binance has not independently confirmed the identity of the attackers. The exchange is cooperating with investigators to establish exactly who was responsible.How did hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance?Binance's initial investigation suggested that the attack may have involved a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. According to the exchange, the attacker may have used access obtained through the laptop to enter a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.However, the investigation later identified additional points of breach. Binance said there was no evidence that its wallet private keys had been leaked. On the Ethereum network, the attacker used a mechanism that allowed a Binance wallet to delegate transaction authority to malicious code.The attack was not limited to Ethereum. Binance wallets on Bitcoin, Tron, Solana, XRP Ledger and several other networks also transferred funds to addresses controlled by the attacker. Most of the $6.36 billion was moved within approximately 20 minutes, suggesting that the attackers had prepared the operation well in advance.Which cryptocurrencies were stolen in the Binance hack?The attack affected 10 blockchain networks and involved several major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT, USDC, XRP and Solana. TRM Labs identified the following major asset movements in its investigation:CryptocurrencyAmount movedEstimated value at the timeBitcoin (BTC)18,270 BTC$1.47 billionEthereum (ETH) and other Ethereum-based assetsMultiple tokens$3.79 billionTether (USDT) on Tron612.7 million USDTPart of $628 million Tron outflowsXRP233.46 million XRP$296 millionSolana (SOL)970,500 SOL$96 millionTRX46.4 million TRXIncluded in Tron outflowsThe Ethereum-related outflows included approximately 200,630 ETH, 1.875 billion USDT, 823 million USDC and 88.5 million RLUSD, along with several other tokens.The attack also affected assets on Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Avalanche and Polygon. The figures represent transfers traced from Binance-attributed wallets. They should not be interpreted as the amount of each cryptocurrency that remains unrecovered. Several stablecoin balances have since been frozen.Where has the stolen $6.3 billion gone?The stolen cryptocurrency was transferred to wallets controlled by the attackers across multiple blockchain networks. Investigators have been tracking these transactions to identify the movement of funds and prevent further transfers. According to TRM Labs, approximately $2.7 billion worth of assets had been frozen by cryptocurrency issuers and other blockchain partners by October 30.This means a substantial portion of the stolen assets has been identified and immobilised. However, freezing cryptocurrency does not necessarily mean the money has been returned to Binance or its customers. The attackers also moved some of the assets between wallets and attempted to convert certain holdings into other cryptocurrencies.Bitcoin and Ethereum account for a significant part of the remaining assets. According to TRM Labs, the attacker still held more than 420,000 Ethereum and approximately 18,270 Bitcoin, worth around $2.4 billion at the time of its assessment.

sources.title: Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than US$2.5 billion frozen - The Straits Times
passages: NEW YORK – Cryptocurrency platform Binance said on Oct 29 it had fallen victim to a major hack that hit around US$6.3 billion (S$8.05 million) in funds, with about half that amount frozen to prevent a massive theft.
Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether – a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT – said his firm froze about US$1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack”.
That would be four times the amount impacted in what had been the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind to date: US$1.5 billion taken in February 2025 from the Bybit platform.
For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform.
Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes.
“We have found no evidence of any private key leaks from wallets,” Binance said, promising to share a detailed technical analysis once investigations were complete.
At about 4am GMT, bitcoin and Ethereum were down 0.8%, recovering after plunges of nearly 5% and nearly 6% respectively.
BNB, native to Binance, was up 2.7% after it tumbled nearly 10%.
The cyberattack on Binance comes as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.

NEW YORK – Cryptocurrency platform Binance said on Oct 29 it had fallen victim to a major hack that hit around US$6.3 billion (S$8.05 million) in funds, with about half that amount frozen to prevent a massive theft. The company said later on its X account for Latin America that “the total estimated impact is around US$6.3 billion”. “We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze the affected assets, with about US$3 billion frozen on-chain so far,” it added. That would be four times the amount impacted in what had been the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind to date: US$1.5 billion taken in February 2025 from the Bybit platform. The Bybit heist was attributed at the time to a group of hackers affiliated with North Korea called TraderTraitor. Blockchain investigation firm TRM Labs said on Oct 29 it had “high confidence” that the Binance hack was also orchestrated by TraderTraitor, citing “robust on and off-chain intelligence”. “Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists,” TRM said. TraderTraitor is believed to be part of Lazarus Group – which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for The Interview, a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. At about 12.30am GMT on Oct 30, Binance said all deposits and withdrawals had been “temporarily suspended while our team conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement”. “This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets,” the company said. The company’s statement on X said an initial investigation suggested the hack involved a compromised laptop belonging to a “DevOps engineer”, allowing the unauthorised party to access a “service container” and execute unauthorised withdrawal transactions. “We have found no evidence of any private key leaks from wallets,” Binance said, promising to share a detailed technical analysis once investigations were complete. Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether – a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT – said his firm froze about US$1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack”. Circle boss Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than US$800 million in USDC. USDT and USDC are both “stablecoins”, or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar. The US Department of Justice and the FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment. For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform. The prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell on the news, except for the stablecoins, which by definition can only fluctuate within tight margins. At about 4am GMT, bitcoin and Ethereum were down 0.8%, recovering after plunges of nearly 5% and nearly 6% respectively. BNB, native to Binance, was up 2.7% after it tumbled nearly 10%. The cyberattack on Binance comes as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols. AFP

coreStoryFacts.text: Datadog slumps 12% and CrowdStrike drops 4% despite a $6.3 billion Binance hack that spotlights the cyber threats both companies are built to stop.
At the same time, CrowdStrike ( NASDAQ:CRWD ) stock is at $249.58, down 4%.
The endpoint security leader remains up 113% YTD.
Network security heavyweight Palo Alto Networks ( NASDAQ:PANW ) is lower as well.
Firewall maker Fortinet ( NASDAQ:FTNT ) is extending a steep slide that followed its latest earnings report.

Coverage of the breach singled out Datadog because crypto exchanges, brokers and fintech firms use its monitoring and security tools, though a hack headline rarely lifts security stocks when the whole technology group is being repriced.
Datadog sells observability software that lets engineering teams track applications, infrastructure and logs, with security and AI tools layered on top.
CrowdStrike builds around its Falcon platform for endpoint, identity and cloud protection.
Palo Alto follows a platform strategy spanning network, cloud and AI security, while Fortinet bases its business in FortiGate firewall appliances and proprietary chips.
The next test for Datadog is whether its upcoming quarterly report shows customers still expanding their cloud usage.
On August 6, the company lifted its 2026 revenue outlook to $4.45 billion to $4.47 billion.
Earnings from the giant cloud operators known as hyperscalers set that repricing in motion.
Alphabet ( NASDAQ:GOOGL ) lost more than $500 billion in market value on October 29 after reporting quarterly free cash flow of negative $9.1 billion.
Wall Street analysts had expected negative $3.5 billion.
Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi argued the broader tech rout owes more to hyperscalers' ballooning artificial intelligence (AI) bills than to one chipmaker's weak outlook.
The platform security company is still up 100% YTD, and a run that steep invites profit-taking in a crowded winner.
A headline-grabbing crypto theft is putting digital defense in the spotlight, yet security-linked software stocks are falling with the rest of tech.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
The bulls could argue that AI-driven threats and breaches like the one at Binance could push security budgets at companies such as CrowdStrike and Datadog higher.
CrowdStrike is falling less than Datadog, and its recent results give the bulls plenty to cite.
The firewall maker remains up 70% YTD, though it had already dropped sharply after its Q3 2026 report on October 28.
On that call, management cited slower conversion of service billings into revenue and gross margin pressure from rising component costs, even as Fortinet's billings grew 29%.

This means customers are not expected to bear the financial burden of the incident, according to the exchange's assurance.The next important development will be Binance's updated proof-of-reserves report, which should help investors assess the exchange's asset backing following the incident.Who hacked Binance and stole $6.3 billion?Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs has attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a hacking unit associated with North Korea.

Most of the $6.36 billion was moved within approximately 20 minutes, suggesting that the attackers had prepared the operation well in advance.Which cryptocurrencies were stolen in the Binance hack?The attack affected 10 blockchain networks and involved several major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT, USDC, XRP and Solana.

Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether – a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT – said his firm froze about US$1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack”.
That would be four times the amount impacted in what had been the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind to date: US$1.5 billion taken in February 2025 from the Bybit platform.
For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform.

That is four times the previous record for such an attack, the $1.5 billion stolen from the Bybit platform in February last year, which was attributed to hackers linked to North Korea.

Tether chief Paolo Ardoino said his company had frozen about $1.6 billion of its USDT stablecoin “related to a potential Binance exchange hack”, and Circle chief Jeremy Allaire said his firm had frozen more than $800 million in USDC.

The figure “may continue to increase” as it works to trace and freeze more assets, it said.

extraction.body: Binance hacked: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, has suffered a massive security breach in which hackers moved approximately $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from its wallets. The attack, which took place on October 29, is being described as the biggest cryptocurrency theft in history. The scale of the incident has raised concerns among cryptocurrency investors. Blockchain investigators have linked the attack to North Korea, while Binance says it has managed to freeze a substantial portion of the affected assets. The incident raises an important question for millions of people who hold Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies on Binance: Could they lose their money because of the hack?135348042Binance has assured customers that their funds are safe and that it will cover all losses arising from the incident. The exchange has also been working with blockchain companies, cryptocurrency issuers and law enforcement agencies to trace and recover the stolen assets.Will you lose your Bitcoin if Binance gets hacked?This is perhaps the biggest concern for Binance customers following the incident. The short answer is that customers do not automatically lose their Bitcoin or other cryptocurrency because of this security breach.Binance has repeatedly assured users that their funds are safe. The exchange has also promised to cover all losses arising from the incident using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and its own funds. The company has not reported evidence that customers' individual account passwords or wallet private keys were leaked in the incident. However, the attack has raised questions about how cryptocurrency exchanges store and protect customer assets.Most large exchanges use hot wallets to process transactions and withdrawals. For investors, the incident is a reminder that holding cryptocurrency on an exchange carries a different set of risks from holding it in a personal wallet.Customers should also be aware that Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals on several networks while it investigated the incident and strengthened its security systems. The exchange said deposits were unaffected and withdrawals were expected to resume within the next day or two.Binance's $1 billion SAFU fund: Is it enough to cover the losses?Binance maintains a Secure Asset Fund for Users, commonly known as SAFU, to protect customers in exceptional circumstances. The fund is worth approximately $1 billion and is designed to provide an additional layer of protection for users.However, the estimated $6.3 billion impact of the latest incident is significantly higher than the fund's reported value.Binance has therefore said it will also use its own resources to cover the losses. This means customers are not expected to bear the financial burden of the incident, according to the exchange's assurance.The next important development will be Binance's updated proof-of-reserves report, which should help investors assess the exchange's asset backing following the incident.Who hacked Binance and stole $6.3 billion?Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs has attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a hacking unit associated with North Korea. The firm said it reached this conclusion with high confidence after examining on-chain transactions and other intelligence. According to TRM Labs, the attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets across 10 different blockchain networks. Most of the transfers took place within around 20 minutes.TraderTraitor is a North Korean hacking operation known for targeting cryptocurrency platforms and digital asset companies. The group has been linked to several major cryptocurrency thefts. The suspected involvement of North Korean hackers is particularly significant because the country has repeatedly been accused of using cyberattacks to generate funds. Its hacking operations have targeted cryptocurrency exchanges, financial institutions and blockchain projects.The group was also linked to the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, which was previously considered the biggest cryptocurrency theft on record. Binance has not independently confirmed the identity of the attackers. The exchange is cooperating with investigators to establish exactly who was responsible.How did hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance?Binance's initial investigation suggested that the attack may have involved a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. According to the exchange, the attacker may have used access obtained through the laptop to enter a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.However, the investigation later identified additional points of breach. Binance said there was no evidence that its wallet private keys had been leaked. On the Ethereum network, the attacker used a mechanism that allowed a Binance wallet to delegate transaction authority to malicious code.The attack was not limited to Ethereum. Binance wallets on Bitcoin, Tron, Solana, XRP Ledger and several other networks also transferred funds to addresses controlled by the attacker. Most of the $6.36 billion was moved within approximately 20 minutes, suggesting that the attackers had prepared the operation well in advance.Which cryptocurrencies were stolen in the Binance hack?The attack affected 10 blockchain networks and involved several major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT, USDC, XRP and Solana. TRM Labs identified the following major asset movements in its investigation:CryptocurrencyAmount movedEstimated value at the timeBitcoin (BTC)18,270 BTC$1.47 billionEthereum (ETH) and other Ethereum-based assetsMultiple tokens$3.79 billionTether (USDT) on Tron612.7 million USDTPart of $628 million Tron outflowsXRP233.46 million XRP$296 millionSolana (SOL)970,500 SOL$96 millionTRX46.4 million TRXIncluded in Tron outflowsThe Ethereum-related outflows included approximately 200,630 ETH, 1.875 billion USDT, 823 million USDC and 88.5 million RLUSD, along with several other tokens.The attack also affected assets on Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Avalanche and Polygon. The figures represent transfers traced from Binance-attributed wallets. They should not be interpreted as the amount of each cryptocurrency that remains unrecovered. Several stablecoin balances have since been frozen.Where has the stolen $6.3 billion gone?The stolen cryptocurrency was transferred to wallets controlled by the attackers across multiple blockchain networks. Investigators have been tracking these transactions to identify the movement of funds and prevent further transfers. According to TRM Labs, approximately $2.7 billion worth of assets had been frozen by cryptocurrency issuers and other blockchain partners by October 30.This means a substantial portion of the stolen assets has been identified and immobilised. However, freezing cryptocurrency does not necessarily mean the money has been returned to Binance or its customers. The attackers also moved some of the assets between wallets and attempted to convert certain holdings into other cryptocurrencies.Bitcoin and Ethereum account for a significant part of the remaining assets. According to TRM Labs, the attacker still held more than 420,000 Ethereum and approximately 18,270 Bitcoin, worth around $2.4 billion at the time of its assessment.

passages: NEW YORK – Cryptocurrency platform Binance said on Oct 29 it had fallen victim to a major hack that hit around US$6.3 billion (S$8.05 million) in funds, with about half that amount frozen to prevent a massive theft.
Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether – a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT – said his firm froze about US$1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack”.
That would be four times the amount impacted in what had been the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind to date: US$1.5 billion taken in February 2025 from the Bybit platform.
For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform.
Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes.
“We have found no evidence of any private key leaks from wallets,” Binance said, promising to share a detailed technical analysis once investigations were complete.
At about 4am GMT, bitcoin and Ethereum were down 0.8%, recovering after plunges of nearly 5% and nearly 6% respectively.
BNB, native to Binance, was up 2.7% after it tumbled nearly 10%.
The cyberattack on Binance comes as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.

Deputies were called to The Cut Bar and Restaurant at 2570 Business Park Court just after 1:45 a.m. to investigate a report of a shooting and stabbing. The sheriff’s office said a private security guard attempted to intervene in a fight between two men when one of them, William Pierre Strong, 41, of Waldorf, threatened the other man with a knife. The security guard tried to take the knife but Strong stabbed the victim in the abdomen, investigators said. The sheriff’s office said that Strong then “appeared to make another attempt to stab the victim.” It was then that the security guard shot Strong, hitting him once in the chest, the sheriff’s office said in a release. The wounded Strong walked out of the bar and collapsed in the parking lot, the sheriff’s office said, and arriving deputies “located him with the knife still in his hand.” The man who was stabbed in the incident suffered injuries that “do not appear to be life-threatening,” according to the sheriff’s office. The case will be presented to the state’s attorney’s office for review, according to a news release. extraction.body: WALDORF, MD — A 41-year-old Waldorf man was fatally shot by a private security guard after stabbing another man during an altercation inside a Waldorf bar early Saturday morning, according to the Charles County Sheriff's Office. William Pierre Strong, 41, died after being shot once in the chest at The Cut Bar & Restaurant, located at 2570 Business Park Court, authorities said. Police said Strong pulled out a knife and threatened the other man. A private security guard assigned to the business attempted to intervene and gain control of Strong's hand and the knife, authorities said. During the confrontation, Strong stabbed the other man once in the abdomen. As Strong appeared to attempt another stabbing, the security guard fired his gun, striking Strong once in the chest, according to investigators. Strong walked outside the establishment before collapsing in the parking lot. Responding deputies found him with the knife still in his hand. Deputies and emergency medical personnel attempted to save his life, but he was pronounced dead at the scene. Deputies responded to the establishment around 1:46 a.m. for reports of a stabbing and shooting. According to the preliminary investigation, two men reportedly got into an altercation inside the bar. Police said Strong pulled out a knife and threatened the other man. A private security guard assigned to the business attempted to intervene and gain control of Strong's hand and the knife, authorities said. During the confrontation, Strong stabbed the other man once in the abdomen. As Strong appeared to attempt another stabbing, the security guard fired his gun, striking Strong once in the chest, according to investigators. Strong walked outside the establishment before collapsing in the parking lot. Responding deputies found him with the knife still in his hand. Deputies and emergency medical personnel attempted to save his life, but he was pronounced dead at the scene. The man who suffered the stab wound was treated for injuries that did not appear to be life-threatening. extraction.body: New Delhi: Amazon has laid off around 250 employees from its devices and services division, with software development roles bearing the brunt of the latest job cuts. The move comes as the company expands its artificial intelligence (AI) investments and makes AI a central part of its engineering operations. The layoffs were announced on Wednesday, the same day Amazon introduced five new devices with Alexa, like a redesigned Echo Show 16 smart screen, an Alexa Photo Frame, and the Echo Time bedside clock. The devices division makes products like Kindle e-readers and Echo smart speakers. Amazon confirmed the job cuts after a Reuters inquiry but did not disclose the number of employees affected. A person familiar with the matter said the reductions involved no more than 250 positions. "We've made the difficult decision to eliminate a small number of roles," an Amazon spokesperson said, adding that the changes would help the company “operate more efficiently and better align with our product roadmap.” Employees Informed Through Early Morning Emails Affected employees were informed about the layoffs through emails and text messages sent early Wednesday morning, according to Reuters. One email cited in the report was sent by Cherie Robinson, a vice president in Amazon's devices and services division. Robinson wrote that the company had conducted "a thorough review of our structure," which led to the decision to cut jobs. Early morning notifications have also featured in previous rounds of job cuts at other technology companies, including Meta and Oracle. The latest reductions come shortly after Amazon published a September memo from its engineering leadership outlining how developers should adapt to the growing use of AI in software development. "We all need to embrace this change and take the time to learn, or we risk being left behind," the memo said, underlining the company's push to make AI a key part of its engineering practices. Fresh Cuts Follow Thousands Of Job Losses The layoffs in the devices division follow Amazon's decision earlier this month to eliminate around 1,000 jobs in its core retail business. The company had also announced 16,000 job cuts in January, following the elimination of 14,000 positions in October last year. Amazon is simultaneously committing substantial resources to AI, with its investment in the technology expected to reach as much as $220 billion this year. The latest layoffs are happening just before the company shares its third-quarter earnings results, which are set to be announced after the markets close on Thursday. Amazon is not alone in reducing its workforce as technology companies reassess their operations and spending priorities. According to reports, more than 135,000 technology jobs have been eliminated this year. Dropbox recently announced plans to cut 9 per cent of its global workforce, while Microsoft has offered voluntary exit options to roughly 60,000 employees, or around one-fourth of its total workforce.

extraction.body: New Delhi: Amazon has laid off around 250 employees from its devices and services division, with software development roles bearing the brunt of the latest job cuts. The move comes as the company expands its artificial intelligence (AI) investments and makes AI a central part of its engineering operations. The layoffs were announced on Wednesday, the same day Amazon introduced five new devices with Alexa, like a redesigned Echo Show 16 smart screen, an Alexa Photo Frame, and the Echo Time bedside clock. The devices division makes products like Kindle e-readers and Echo smart speakers. Amazon confirmed the job cuts after a Reuters inquiry but did not disclose the number of employees affected. A person familiar with the matter said the reductions involved no more than 250 positions. "We've made the difficult decision to eliminate a small number of roles," an Amazon spokesperson said, adding that the changes would help the company “operate more efficiently and better align with our product roadmap.” Employees Informed Through Early Morning Emails Affected employees were informed about the layoffs through emails and text messages sent early Wednesday morning, according to Reuters. One email cited in the report was sent by Cherie Robinson, a vice president in Amazon's devices and services division. Robinson wrote that the company had conducted "a thorough review of our structure," which led to the decision to cut jobs. Early morning notifications have also featured in previous rounds of job cuts at other technology companies, including Meta and Oracle. The latest reductions come shortly after Amazon published a September memo from its engineering leadership outlining how developers should adapt to the growing use of AI in software development. "We all need to embrace this change and take the time to learn, or we risk being left behind," the memo said, underlining the company's push to make AI a key part of its engineering practices. Fresh Cuts Follow Thousands Of Job Losses The layoffs in the devices division follow Amazon's decision earlier this month to eliminate around 1,000 jobs in its core retail business. The company had also announced 16,000 job cuts in January, following the elimination of 14,000 positions in October last year. Amazon is simultaneously committing substantial resources to AI, with its investment in the technology expected to reach as much as $220 billion this year. The latest layoffs are happening just before the company shares its third-quarter earnings results, which are set to be announced after the markets close on Thursday. Amazon is not alone in reducing its workforce as technology companies reassess their operations and spending priorities. According to reports, more than 135,000 technology jobs have been eliminated this year. Dropbox recently announced plans to cut 9 per cent of its global workforce, while Microsoft has offered voluntary exit options to roughly 60,000 employees, or around one-fourth of its total workforce.

The world's biggest crypto exchange said hackers had gained access to $6.3bn (£4.7bn) worth of digital assets, and while it has frozen about half, many remained in the hands of the thieves. These stories are full of specialist language that people outside the industry struggle to understand. So if you're unsure what the blockchain or a crypto echange or even a cryptocurrency itself are, here are some key terms and what they mean. While many may struggle with the finer points of crypto, pretty much everyone has heard of its most famous product: Bitcoin. But what actually is it? Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is to say a type of digital currency. Unlike traditional currencies, Bitcoin is not controlled by centralised financial institutions. This makes it popular for people who think decentralisation can bring financial freedom, but it also makes it extremely volatile with it rising and falling in value at the whim of Bitcoin buyers and sellers. Donald Trump has pledged to make the US the "crypto capital of the world" - backtracking on his previous claim that Bitcoin was a "scam" . Its price topped a much-awaited threshold of $100,000 in December 2024, then rose to $120,000 in July 2025 as US politicians prepared to debate bills to regulate digital assets. In October 2025, Bitcoin hit an all-time high of around $126,000, buoyed by a continued wave of institutional investment and positive market sentiment. But it has been known to plummet in value just as quickly as it spikes. In early February 2026, its price dipped below $65,000 to effectively wipe out gains achieved under President Trump. Against the backdrop of these frequent price fluctuations, speculation continues about the true identity of Bitcoin's mysterious inventor known only as Satoshi Nakamoto. Brit says he is not elusive Bitcoin creator named by New York Times Seven wild moments from the turbulent story of Bitcoin Blockchain is the technology underpinning all cryptocurrencies, and many related products like non-fungible tokens (NFTs). In essence, it is a virtual spreadsheet on which all the buying and selling of crypto is recorded. They are arranged in blocks linked together in a giant chain - hence the name. Every cryptocurrency transaction is individually recorded onto the blockchain by a huge network of volunteers verifying its authenticity by using computer programmes. The incentive to do this for Bitcoin's network is that the first person to validate transactions is rewarded in Bitcoin. This potentially lucrative process, known as mining, is also controversial because of the incredible amount of energy , external used as people the world over race to be the first to successfully update the blockchain. A crypto exchange is the digital platform where investors can buy, sell and trade cryptocurrencies. Similar to traditional investing, a crypto exchange acts as a brokerage where people can transfer traditional money, like pounds or dollars, in exchange for cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin or Ethereum. Most transactions are accompanied by fees. Binance is the world's biggest, which is part of what makes the hack so monumental. A crypto wallet is a place where investors hold their cryptocurrency. There are two types, a hot wallet and a cold wallet. Cold wallets are physical devices like specially designed USB sticks that store crypto offline typically for safer and longer term storage. Man told he can't recover £598m of Bitcoin from landfill site Ethereum is used to describe both the second largest cryptocurrency after Bitcoin, represented by the Ether token, and the blockchain underpinning it. This supports an array of different applications and digital assets, such as non-fungible tokens. It functions in a similar way to Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, but in 2022 switched to a greener operating system requiring less computers and energy . A spot Bitcoin ETF buys the cryptocurrency directly, "on the spot", at its current price, throughout the day. While some ETFs already contained Bitcoin indirectly, the US approved several spot Bitcoin ETFs in January 2024. This allowed new investors, such as investment management firms like Blackrock and Fidelity, to enter the speculative world of Bitcoin without having to worry about digital wallets or navigating crypto exchanges. Cryptocurrency firm Terraform, behind the crashed TerraUSD and Luna tokens, files for bankruptcy XRP is a cryptocurrency used by a platform called the XRP Ledger. It was created by the co-founders of financial services company Ripple Labs in 2012 as a cheaper, faster alternative to Bitcoin. The cryptocurrency has a fixed supply of 100 billion coins, which were created when it launched. Much of it is held by Ripple and periodically released into circulation. This has been credited with allowing many transactions to take place simultaneously, at high speed and low cost - making it appealing to financial institutions or for processes like cross-border payments. But as with other cryptocurrencies, XRP has received regulatory scrutiny and seen sudden, sharp declines in value . Donald Trump has pledged to make the US the "crypto capital of the world" - backtracking on his previous claim that Bitcoin was a "scam" . Its price topped a much-awaited threshold of $100,000 in December 2024, then rose to $120,000 in July 2025 as US politicians prepared to debate bills to regulate digital assets. In October 2025, Bitcoin hit an all-time high of around $126,000, buoyed by a continued wave of institutional investment and positive market sentiment. But it has been known to plummet in value just as quickly as it spikes. In early February 2026, its price dipped below $65,000 to effectively wipe out gains achieved under President Trump. Against the backdrop of these frequent price fluctuations, speculation continues about the true identity of Bitcoin's mysterious inventor known only as Satoshi Nakamoto. In essence, it is a virtual spreadsheet on which all the buying and selling of crypto is recorded. They are arranged in blocks linked together in a giant chain - hence the name. Every cryptocurrency transaction is individually recorded onto the blockchain by a huge network of volunteers verifying its authenticity by using computer programmes. The incentive to do this for Bitcoin's network is that the first person to validate transactions is rewarded in Bitcoin. This potentially lucrative process, known as mining, is also controversial because of the incredible amount of energy , external used as people the world over race to be the first to successfully update the blockchain.
